points.description: States that the compiler replaces each call to the inline function with a copy of the function's code, so the code is inserted at every place the function is called. Equivalent wording (e.g. 'the body is expanded/pasted in at each call site') earns the mark. A vague answer such as 'it makes the function faster' without the copy-at-each-call idea earns no marks.

rubric.notes: This is a single idea, so it is one all-or-nothing point worth the full 5 marks. A full-mark answer says the function's code is copied or inserted at each call site. An answer that describes only a normal function call, or gives no mechanism, gets no marks.
